fn solve(r1: Int, c1: Int, r2: Int, c2: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires (1 <= r1)
  requires (r1 <= 8)
  requires (1 <= c1)
  requires (c1 <= 8)
  requires (1 <= r2)
  requires (r2 <= 8)
  requires (1 <= c2)
  requires (c2 <= 8)
  ensures (len(result) == 3)
  ensures (result[0] == (if ((r1 == r2) and (c1 == c2)) then 0 else if ((r1 == r2) or (c1 == c2)) then 1 else 2))
  ensures (result[1] == (if ((r1 == r2) and (c1 == c2)) then 0 else if ((if (r1 >= r2) then (r1 - r2) else (r2 - r1)) == (if (c1 >= c2) then (c1 - c2) else (c2 - c1))) then 1 else if (((r1 + c1) % 2) == ((r2 + c2) % 2)) then 2 else 0))
  ensures (result[2] == (if ((if (r1 >= r2) then (r1 - r2) else (r2 - r1)) >= (if (c1 >= c2) then (c1 - c2) else (c2 - c1))) then if (r1 >= r2) then (r1 - r2) else (r2 - r1) else if (c1 >= c2) then (c1 - c2) else (c2 - c1)))
  effects pure
  example (solve(0, 0, 0, 0) == [])
